Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of October 19 to October 23:

, North America’s largest flat-rolled steel producer, is set to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Monday, with investors weighing an expected return to profitability against growing uncertainty surrounding its Canadian subsidiary, Stelco.

In Q2 2026, Cleveland-Cliffs reported revenue of $5.23B, slightly above the $5.15B consensus estimate. The company posted a net loss attributable to shareholders of $145M, or $0.20 per share. Despite pressure from lower average steel selling prices and operational headwinds, management highlighted cost-reduction initiatives and stable shipments to core automotive customers.

Stelco remains a key source of uncertainty. Cleveland-Cliffs shares fell nearly 8% on September 28 amid reports that Stelco planned to halt operations at a major Ontario processing facility. CEO Lourenco Goncalves has described the layoffs as temporary and said the company intends to rehire workers. On October 16, the Canadian government said it was considering nationalization and other measures amid concerns over Cleveland-Cliffs’ workforce commitments following its acquisition of Stelco.
Wall Street rates Cleveland-Cliffs a Hold, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system assigns the stock a Buy.
: CLF has topped EPS expectations in 5 of the past 8 quarters, beating revenue estimates in 4 of those reports.

is all set to report its Q3 2026 results after Tuesday’s close, with investors weighing its advertising growth and margin outlook against intensifying competition from YouTube and a series of analyst downgrades. The stock is down approximately 25% YTD, raising the stakes for its latest results.

In Q2 2026, Netflix reported revenue of $12.56B, up 13.4% Y/Y, while diluted EPS of $0.80 edged past the $0.79 consensus. For Q3, management guided for revenue of approximately $12.86B and EPS of $0.82, below prior Street expectations, triggering a post-earnings sell-off. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance stands at $51.0B–$51.4B, with an operating margin target of 31.5%. Advertising remains a key growth driver, with the business expected to generate approximately $3B in revenue in 2026, roughly double the prior year.

Recent analyst actions have highlighted concerns about engagement and competition. Wells Fargo downgraded Netflix to Underweight in September, citing a potential decline in viewing hours for its top originals, while HSBC cut its rating to Hold from Buy and lowered its price target to $76. Deutsche Bank subsequently upgraded the stock to Buy with a $95 target, and Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating with a $90 target. Netflix also announced plans to cut approximately 1,000 jobs on October 14, adding to investor focus on cost discipline as content spending rises.
Wall Street rates Netflix a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system assigns a more cautious Hold.
: Netflix has exceeded EPS and revenue estimates in 6 of the past 8 quarters.

is slated to report its Q3 2026 results after Wednesday’s close, with investors focused on automotive margins, free cash flow, and the Cybercab rollout after quarterly deliveries exceeded consensus. Updates on robotaxi expansion, autonomous-driving monetization, and Optimus are also expected to feature prominently.

In Q2 2026, Tesla reported revenue of $28.24B, up 25.5% Y/Y and above the $26.42B consensus, while EPS of $0.33 missed estimates of $0.50. Automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits was 16.3%, as credit revenue fell to $146M from $439M. In Q3, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles, down 2.1% Y/Y but approximately 25,000 above consensus, while energy storage deployments reached 13.7 GWh, up more than 40% Y/Y.

Recent developments have put Tesla’s autonomous-driving ambitions and regulatory risks in focus. The Cybercab fleet in Austin has expanded, with Dallas identified as the next potential market, while a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration review opened October 9 is examining alleged school-zone speed-limit violations involving approximately 1,000 Tesla robotaxi vehicles. Tesla is required to respond by October 30. The company also unveiled its redesigned Roadster, featuring a SpaceX-linked rocket-thruster concept, with production targeted for 2028, well beyond its original 2020 delivery target. The Roadster’s performance claims and Cybercab’s regulatory progress add to the range of issues investors may weigh alongside quarterly results.
Wall Street maintains a Buy consensus, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating is Hold.
: Tesla has exceeded EPS in 3 and revenue estimates in 5 of the past 8 quarters.

is set to report its Q3 2026 results after Wednesday’s close, with investors weighing continued advertising growth against elevated AI infrastructure spending. The report also comes amid a major push into frontier AI models as the company seeks to strengthen its position against OpenAI and Anthropic.

In Q2 2026, Meta reported revenue of $60.80B, up 28% Y/Y and above the $60.22B consensus. Advertising revenue rose 27% to $59.36B, supported by a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in average price per ad. Adjusted EPS of $6.18 fell short of the $7.19 consensus. Management guided for Q3 revenue of $61B–$64B and reaffirmed its full-year 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $125B–$145B, largely directed toward AI infrastructure.

Recent developments have centered on Meta’s AI strategy. Last week, the company unveiled its Muse Wonder models, which it said were competitive with leading AI systems on independent benchmarks. Meta also released an open-weight version of Muse Spark, while keeping its more advanced Wonder models closed, marking a shift from the open approach associated with its Llama models. Reports also indicated that Meta had reduced internal use of Anthropic’s Claude Code as it expanded its own AI tools.
Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy consensus, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating is Hold.
: META has exceeded revenue estimates in 8 straight quarters, missing EPS just once in that time span.

is scheduled to report its Q1 2027 results before Thursday’s open, with investors focused on the impact of tariffs, higher input costs, and rising shipping expenses. Management has warned that core EPS could decline at least 5% Y/Y in the quarter as cost pressures weigh on first-half performance.

In Q4 FY2026, Procter & Gamble reported revenue of $21.20B, up 1.5% Y/Y but below the $21.38B consensus, while adjusted EPS of $1.43 topped estimates of $1.41. For FY2027, the company forecast adjusted EPS of $6.89–$7.11, below the $7.04 analyst consensus, and revenue of $85.1B–$86.8B, also below Street expectations. Management has flagged approximately $1B in pretax tariff costs and introduced mid-single-digit price increases on roughly 25% of its U.S. products to help offset the impact.

Recent analyst actions have offered some support. Earlier this month, Evercore ISI upgraded the stock to Outperform from In Line and raised its price target to $166 from $161, while Citigroup lifted its target to $180 from $170 and maintained a Buy rating. However, higher oil and shipping costs linked to Middle East tensions add to the cost pressures facing the company.
Wall Street rates the stock a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating holds a more cautious Hold.
: PG has topped EPS expectations in 8 consecutive quarters, beating revenue estimates in 4 of those reports.

, the global payments and premium lifestyle brand, is scheduled to report its Q3 2026 results before the market opens on Friday, October 23. Shares have come under pressure in recent months as investors weigh expense growth, regulatory scrutiny and the company’s efforts to position itself for AI-driven commerce.

In Q2 2026, American Express posted EPS of $4.53, beating the $4.40 consensus by $0.13, with revenue of $19.64 billion up 10% year-over-year. Card member spending growth accelerated to 10% on an FX-adjusted basis, driven by affluent consumer resilience and strong T&E spending. Management reaffirmed the full-year 2026 guidance of revenue growth of 9% to 10% and EPS of $17.30 to $17.90. For Q3, network volumes are expected to grow 8.6% Y/Y, and discount revenues are projected up 8%; with rising operating expenses, the primary margin headwind that analysts are flagging heading into Friday’s print.

On the product front, American Express launched the next generation of Amex Corporate, combining corporate cards, integrated expense management software, and a mobile app with AI capabilities. The company also published its Intent Intelligence framework last week, outlining an approach to capturing and authenticating customers’ purchase intent before AI agents execute transactions. The framework could help address trust and payment-security challenges as agentic commerce develops, although its commercial impact remains to be established.
However, the Federal Reserve issued an enforcement action against American Express over anti-money-laundering deficiencies in October, adding a compliance headline risk heading into Friday’s call.

Analyst price-target reductions have added to the cautious backdrop. Barclays lowered its target to $342 from $364 while maintaining an Equal Weight rating. Citigroup cut its target to $340 from $355, retaining a Neutral rating, while BTIG reduced its target to $230 from $315 in September and maintained a Sell rating.
Wall Street rates the stock a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating holds a more cautious Hold.
: The company has topped EPS and revenue expectations in 6 of the past 8 quarters.
